answer: A staking bond tied to verifiable work raises the cost of fake identities: each agent must lock funds in a vault before it can act, and the bond is slashed if its claims prove false. One operator running many fake agents must fund every vault, so the attack cost grows with each identity instead of staying near zero. Reputation then accrues slowly over a long horizon, so a fresh fake cannot instantly match a trusted agent, and crossing that ridge of accumulated trust takes sustained honest work, not just new keys.
